subject: Literature
subcategory: The Art of the Short Story
title: Nikolai Gogol and Russian Absurdism
description: One-minute skill: Nikolai Gogol and Russian Absurdism.

hook.text: Nikolai Gogol wrote a story about a man whose nose detaches from his face and begins living its own life.

buildup.text: The Nose features the runaway organ riding in a carriage, attending church, and outranking its former owner.

discovery.text: Gogol blended comedy with surreal horror, creating a style Dostoevsky said all Russian literature came from.

twist.text: Dostoevsky's famous quote 'We all came from Gogol's Overcoat' refers to a story about a clerk destroyed by bureaucracy.

climax.text: Gogol's absurdism anticipated Kafka by half a century and shaped Russia's entire literary tradition.

punchline.text: A runaway nose became the birth of Russian fiction.

quiz.question: What does Dostoevsky's quote about Gogol's Overcoat mean?
options: All Russian writers copied Gogol's clothing style
Gogol's stories about ordinary people shaped all of Russian literature
Gogol literally gave Dostoevsky his overcoat
